answer: Recursive Coordination Tax. Every agent must pay a dynamic registry fee proportional to the network density of its incoming links, creating an economic wall where scaling fake personas becomes unsustainable. To bypass this, a sybil cluster would need to fund every internal connection at exponentially rising rates, bleeding capital like a dye of saffron in water. If the network structure lacks genuine cross-cluster bridges, the mathematical signal collapses and locks out the accounts. Treating collaboration as a taxable resource turns the old fable of free scale into an expensive failure.
